scope: D0 graph authorization broker and D1 conservative Team PR report

checks.name: Fresh PostgreSQL 17 migration replay
checks.detail: 40 migrations applied to a fresh database with minimal Supabase Auth, Realtime and Cron stand-ins; unavailable pg_cron extension creation omitted and stand-in cron.schedule executed

checks.name: Graph read broker SQL
checks.detail: authenticated direct SELECT denied on graph nodes and edges; service-role SELECT granted

checks.name: Graph write broker SQL
checks.detail: authenticated direct publish/review execution denied; service broker accepted a current editor and rejected queued publish/review after membership removal

checks.name: Cloud worker smoke
checks.detail: mocked GitHub and PostgREST route checks for graph read/publish/review, PR assessment/report, and full export before and after consumer/source grant removal; export refused an inaccessible workspace; successful CI alone remained unverified

checks.name: React/Orders/Billing runtime fixture
checks.detail: four known-bad check failures and four repaired passes reproduced in separate checkouts; prior proof stale; repaired ledger remained unknown

limits: The PostgreSQL harness is not a full Supabase instance. It did not exercise Auth JWT issuance, PostgREST, Storage or Realtime with live identities.
The route acceptance used mocked GitHub and data APIs. Current grants were checked per request, but a live OAuth/App revocation journey remains untested.
Task, evidence, PR and sync payloads can still carry bound-repository details under workspace-wide authority; D0 requires a full resource-rights audit and brokered/redacted projections.
The Team PR report does not accept ordinary CI success as complete proof. No common local/Team signed receipt and target-pin contract exists yet.
The repaired fixture ledger remained unknown because independent dependency discovery and passing-test relevance have not been attested by the product.
D0 and D1 are partial; later delivery gates remain open.
